verdicts.reasoning: The proposal concerns the probative weight/value of evidence, whereas the label-similar candidates define procedural rules (Rules of Evidence), a proof standard (Some Evidence), and a contract doctrine (Parol Evidence Rule) — none captures evidentiary value.

An 'evidentiary position' is an argued stance a party takes on evidence, which differs from the candidates' definitions of a motion (Evidentiary Motions), a formal protest (Evidentiary Objection), and the goals of presenting evidence (Evidentiary Objectives) despite the near-identical labels.
The proposal uses 'aid' meaning to help/facilitate, a pure string collision with the candidate AIDS (the disease) and place-name languages (Haida, Maidu), whose definitions are wholly unrelated.

'Document drafting' denotes the activity of drafting, whereas the closest candidate 'Draft Document Version' defines an artifact (an intermediate version of a document) — an activity versus a thing, so the definitions do not align.
'Viable' (feasible/meritorious claims) is a near-homograph of the top candidate 'Liable' (legally responsible), but their definitions describe entirely different concepts.

'Case type' (criminal vs. personal-injury categorization of a matter) only shares the word 'type' with candidates Asset Type, charge_type, and tax_type, whose definitions concern assets, billing, and taxes.
'Client advice' (advising a client) shares the word 'advice' with Negligent Advice, but that candidate defines a professional-negligence claim for failing to advise, not the advice itself.
'Defense attorney' (defense counsel role) shares the token 'attorney' with candidates defining fees, deceit, and responsible/relationship attorneys, none of which denotes the defense-side lawyer.
'Audio' as a sensory medium is a string collision with Auditor and Audit (financial examination) and Audiobook (a copyrighted recording), whose definitions are unrelated.
'Distance' as a perception factor in witness credibility is a coincidental substring of candidates Instance, Nuisance, and Deal Stance, whose definitions have nothing to do with spatial distance.
'Case Extension' (prolonging litigation as a delay tactic) shares 'extension' with the candidates, but all of them define contractual term-extension clauses, an unrelated concept.
'Hearing practice' here means rehearsing/simulating hearings for training, sharing only the word 'practice' with candidates defining pleadings, lending, and mediation practice areas.
'Law students' is a specific subtype not equal to the generic candidate 'Student' (any enrolled individual), and the top-scored 'Student Loan' is an unrelated financial-product definition.

'Legal education' (educating lawyers) is the inverse of the label-similar candidate 'Education Law' (the body of law governing schools), so despite the word overlap the definitions describe different things.
A 'jury instruction guide' (JIG) is a published reference compilation of pattern instructions, which is distinct from the candidate 'Jury Instructions' (the actual directions a judge gives the jury).
'Task' (a subdivided unit of work) collides only phonetically with the place-name candidates Tak, Tabuk, and Lasko, whose definitions are geographic.
'Attempt' (to try ADR) shares the stem with candidate 'Attempted', but that candidate defines the criminal-law concept of an attempted crime, an unrelated meaning.
